chapter: Alma Hightower and other women musicians
title: Irma Young and Lester Young's father
summary: Howard says Irma Young never played jobs with him and that Mr. Young taught a little but did not play.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: What about Lester Young's sister? She was a pianist--what's her name, you remember? Irma Young?
Do you know whether she played any jobs?
Did she ever play any jobs that you know of?
Never heard of her playing with a band.
Yeah. All right. I was just wondering 'cause I knew she was a good pianist.
Yeah, but she didn't play none.
Uh-huh. Do you know whether the father ever played any jobs?
He didn't ever play any jobs?
No (laugh). Lester Young was too busy--he was busy--he was busy gettin' himself together. He couldn't play. I know him, too.
Uh-huh. Well, I know you did. You were right next to him for a long time, there, at the Union.
But he was teaching? Other than the family? Did he do a little teaching?
Teaching, yeah. Did a little teaching.
When you say 'getting himself together,' there, you mean, just in life?
Yeah, in life, and in tryin' to get his horn together and get everything together.
